explanation: The fiercest winds whirl in the eyewall around it. Hurricanes, typhoons and tropical cyclones are the same kind of storm, named differently in different oceans.

claims.text: The eye of a hurricane or typhoon usually has calm winds and often clear skies.
The strongest winds, torrential rain and frequent lightning belong to the eyewall and rain bands, not the eye.
A hurricane's strongest winds blow in the eyewall around the eye.
Hurricanes, typhoons and tropical cyclones are the same type of storm, given different names in different ocean basins.
